proposals.reason: Literal English is ungrammatical (“Biographies the Thirty-first”); the Chinese is a standard chapter title.

proposals.before: Eleven years later, in Zhenghe 3 (90 BCE), Ershi took seventy thousand horse out of Wuyuan against the Xiongnu and crossed the Zhiju River.
proposals.after: Eleven years later, in Zhenghe 3 (90 BCE), Ershi led seventy thousand cavalry out of Wuyuan against the Xiongnu and crossed the Zhiju River.
proposals.reason: Chinese 將七萬騎 means he led seventy thousand cavalry; idiomatic “took seventy thousand horse” is ungrammatical and obscures the military sense.

decisions.reason: 傳第三十一 is the standard ordinal biography title; “Biographies the Thirty-first” is ungrammatical, and “Biography Thirty-first” correctly renders the Chinese without inventing content.
This unit is only 孫猛, kinship plus given name; “Zhang Meng” invents the surname 張 not present here (s0130’s 騫孫猛 confirms grandson Meng, not a written 張).
Literal must track 孫猛 alone; inserting Zhang invents a surname absent from this unit, while “Grandson Meng” matches the Chinese.
將七萬騎 means he led seventy thousand cavalry; “took seventy thousand horse” is ungrammatical and weakens the command sense already clear in the Chinese.
